thread:
Sanjay Patel: quick heads-up — after the RBAC refactor deploy last night a subset of job-runner-prod tasks are showing analytics:write granted. they should only have analytics:read. noticed it from unexpected s3 PUT spikes and a handful of completed jobs that wrote interim metrics to analytics buckets. KMS decrypt logs are weirdly absent for those PUTs. seems like the temp-allowlist path may have bypassed policy scoping. can we triage now?

Elaine Wong: @Sanjay thanks — which deploy? can you paste the refactor PR?

Sanjay Patel: PR 4321, merged @ 03:14 UTC.

Sanjay Patel: logs (sanitized):
```
2026-03-19T03:22:11Z job-runner-prod-42 started task id=abc123 scope=analytics:read
2026-03-19T03:22:12Z AUTHZ allow via temp-allowlist user=svc-job-runner role=temp-bridge -> granted analytics:write
2026-03-19T03:22:13Z s3 PUT bucket=redwood-analytics key=tmp/metrics-abc.json size=4.2KB
2026-03-19T03:22:13Z KMS decrypt request id=none found
```

Marco Ruiz: ugh. that AUTHZ line implies temp-allowlist returned broader permission set than expected. @Elaine can you check the allowlist config in the deploy? maybe defaulted to wildcard.

Elaine Wong: checking now. Config in infra repo shows: `temp_allowlist: ["analytics:*"]` — that looks like a botched merge. intended was `analytics:read`.

Nadia Chen: if that's true we should revoke the temp-allowlist immediately and block further writes. Recommend: 1) patch allowlist to explicit read-only 2) apply emergency deny policy to job-runner-prod service role 3) rotate any short-lived creds that issued tokens with elevated scope.

Sanjay Patel: I'm applying the deny policy to the service role now. patching repo and will submit an emergency revert PR.

sec-bot: automated alert — policy-change detected: applied deny_policy/service/job-runner-prod @ 03:23:05 UTC (actor: Sanjay Patel).

Marco Ruiz: good. Nadia — can you query KMS audit store for decrypt attempts between 03:10-03:30 UTC? we need to confirm whether any customer data was actually decrypted and exfiltrated.

Nadia Chen: running query now. if KMS logs are missing for those requests maybe the decrypts used a fallback CMK or a cached plaintext path. I'll check both KMS logs and runtime KV cache evictions.

Sanjay Patel: FYI, I found two PUTs that targeted an internal analytics bucket (non-prod customer sandbox) — not customer PII buckets. still bad, but scope contained.

Elaine Wong: PR 4321 reverted (emergency) and new PR 4330 submitted that restores strict scoping. patch will be applied after quick review.

oncall-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0330 "temp-allowlist widened permissions during RBAC refactor" severity=P2. responders: @Nadia Chen, @Marco Ruiz, @Sanjay Patel.

Marco Ruiz: next steps: 1) verify deny policy held 2) confirm no KMS decrypts for customer PII 3) run retrospective on allowlist codepath to add unit tests and CI gating 4) add alert for any temp-allowlist returns with wildcard scopes.

Nadia Chen: KMS query preliminary: no decrypt events for production customer keys in that window. there are decrypts for sandbox CMKs (expected by some jobs). digging KV cache now.

Sanjay Patel: thanks everyone — I'll keep the deny policy in place until we have a full postmortem. starting a short blameless write-up and will attach timeline + logs to the incident ticket.

Elaine Wong: nice catch, @Sanjay. little reminder: avoid allowing `:*` in allowlists and add a linter rule.

Marco Ruiz: agreed. also let's add a quick audit query that alerts if any service role performs a privileged write it historically never did.

Sanjay Patel: will follow up in INC-2026-0330 with remediation checklist and timeline. :thumbsup:
